g.text: How much drug leaves through the kidney unchanged?

text.style: font-size: 15px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #536779

g.text: Urinary recovery of parent drug (% of administered dose) • Reported values and bounds; mainly oral dosing

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 12px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #9b6415
font-size: 13px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #17324d

g.text: Gabapentin: renal elimination of essentially all absorbed drug; this is not 100% of the swallowed dose.

text.style: font-size: 13px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #17324d

g.text: Metformin: ≈90% of absorbed drug recovered renally in 24 h. Digoxin: 50–70% of an intravenous dose.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 13px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #17324d

g.text: * Parent-drug percentages do not capture active-metabolite accumulation or all effects of CKD on drug exposure.

text.style: font-size: 12px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #17324d

g.text: Venlafaxine and risperidone are key examples. Low unchanged excretion does not establish safety or remove dose restrictions.

text.style: font-size: 11px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #536779

g.text: Ranges/bounds are shown as reported; they are not confidence intervals. “Not detected” and “negligible” are not plotted as zero.

text.style: font-size: 10px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #536779

g.text: Sources: product labels and human pharmacokinetic studies • Full per-drug links and study notes: renal-excretion-sources.md • Reviewed 16 Nov 2026
